spec.title: Tabletop bottle pick-and-place, A to B, 10 per minute
spec.summary: A fixed arm picks a closed 300 g plastic bottle (Ø0.07 m × 0.22 m tall) standing upright at point A on a 0.75 m high table, and places it upright at point B 0.6 m away on the same table, with ±5 mm placement accuracy. It runs at 10 bottles per minute, so each cycle is 6 s.
spec.frame: World frame: metres, z up, origin on the floor. Table top at z = 0.75 m.

actions.description: Approach from above, grip the bottle body and lift it clear
Carry the bottle upright 0.6 m to above B
Lower it, set it upright within 5 mm and release
Go back above A for the next bottle

markers.name: Point A (pick)
markers.note: Bottle stands upright on the table top

markers.name: Point B (place)
markers.note: 0.6 m from A along y, on the table top

spec.duty_cycle: Continuous, 600 cycles per hour, one shift per day assumed
spec.payload_description: Closed plastic bottle, cylinder Ø0.07 m × 0.22 m, 0.3 kg. Picked and placed upright with a parallel gripper around the body.
assumptions: A and B are placed symmetrically 0.5 m in front of the origin and 0.6 m apart along y. Their real positions were not given.
The bottle must stay upright from pick to place, as the bottle_pose answer indicates.
It is gripped around its body by a parallel gripper with 2 contacts, with friction coefficient 0.4 (plastic on gripper pads).
10 per minute means a 6 s cycle: 600 cycles per hour in continuous running.
Approach height is 0.1 m above the bottle and clearance is 0.05 m.
No robot base position was given, so the tool places the robot.

calc.note: Governing point: point_a+approach; distance from the base mounting point to the task point; each marker and the same point raised by the approach height.
Nearest task point to the base; the robot must be able to fold in this far or stay clear.
Tool mass estimated as 0.3 + 0.15 x object mass (capped at 3 kg for objects up to 10 kg).

calc.formula: v = d / (T_move - t_a), t_a = T_move / 3, T_move = T_budget d_longest / sum_d
calc.note: Time budget (cycle time minus dwell) split over the moves by distance; moves are the legs between task points, the return to the first point and the approach up/down at each pick/place.
Acceleration from the cycle time (accel phase = 1/3 of the move).
Friction grip: normal force per contact so friction carries weight plus acceleration. Acceleration a = 0.533 m/s^2 from tcp_accel.
Repeatability is taken as half the positional accuracy tolerance.

markers.name: Point A (pick)
markers.note: Bottle stands upright on the table top

markers.name: Point B (place)
markers.note: 0.6 m from A along y, on the table top

scene.notes: Two tables (A and B) leave the 0.3 m circle around the floor-mounted robot base free.

robot.name: 4-axis tabletop bottle mover
robot.rationale: The task asks for a fixed arm, and a serial arm can reach points A and B with one base yaw swing while keeping the tool pointing down. Four axes are enough: yaw, shoulder, elbow and wrist pitch hold the bottle upright, and a round bottle doesn't need tool roll. A parallel gripper with about 6 cm of stroke closes around the 7 cm bottle. The main limit is reach: the far task points are close to full extension, so the links must be long enough that the arm still has some bend there, which helps stiffness and repeatability.

v2_spec.title: Tabletop bottle pick-and-place, A to B, 15 per minute
v2_spec.summary: A fixed arm mounted on the table top between A and B picks a closed 300 g plastic bottle (Ø0.07 m × 0.22 m tall) standing upright at point A on a 0.75 m high table, and places it upright at point B 0.6 m away on the same table, with ±5 mm placement accuracy. Each cycle takes 4 s (15 bottles per minute).
v2_spec.frame: World frame: metres, z up, origin on the floor. Table top at z = 0.75 m.

actions.description: Approach from above, grip the bottle body and lift it clear
Carry the bottle upright 0.6 m to above B
Lower it, set it upright within 5 mm and release
Go back above A for the next bottle

markers.name: Point A (pick)
markers.note: Bottle stands upright on the table top

markers.name: Point B (place)
markers.note: 0.6 m from A along y, on the table top

v2_spec.duty_cycle: Continuous, 900 cycles per hour, one shift per day assumed
v2_spec.payload_description: Closed plastic bottle, cylinder Ø0.07 m × 0.22 m, 0.3 kg. Picked and placed upright with a parallel gripper around the body.
assumptions: A and B are placed symmetrically 0.5 m in front of the origin and 0.6 m apart along y. Their real positions were not given.
The bottle must stay upright from pick to place, as the bottle_pose answer indicates.
It is gripped around its body by a parallel gripper with 2 contacts, with friction coefficient 0.4 (plastic on gripper pads).
A 4 s cycle means 15 bottles per minute: 900 cycles per hour in continuous running.
Approach height is 0.1 m above the bottle and clearance is 0.05 m.
The robot base is mounted at table-top height (z = 0.75 m) midway between A and B, at (0.5, 0, 0.75), on a mounting plate bridging the two table sections.

v2_robot_rationale: The task asks for a fixed arm, now mounted on the table top between A and B. A serial arm can reach both points with one base yaw swing while keeping the tool pointing down. Four axes are enough: yaw, shoulder, elbow and wrist pitch hold the bottle upright, and a round bottle doesn't need tool roll. A parallel gripper with about 6 cm of stroke closes around the 7 cm bottle. Because the base sits at table height, the base column is short (0.16 m), so the shoulder stays at about the same height as before. The shorter 4 s cycle needs faster joints and more acceleration.
v2_change_summary: The robot now sits on the table top at (0.5, 0, 0.75) between A and B instead of on the floor, and each cycle now takes 4 s (900 cycles per hour).
